idiom_name: BullMQ failed set with schema-validated typed payload and attempts/backoff
implementation_notes: BullMQ models the invalid channel as the job's failed set: a processor that throws moves the job there, retention is governed by the queue's auto-removal settings and the retry policy by attempts/backoff, and the documented way to refuse a retry is a custom backoffStrategy returning -1. TypeScript contributes the validation front: parse job.data into a discriminated union or a schema-validated type before doing any work and throw a dedicated InvalidPayload error when parsing fails, so the failed set holds exactly the unprocessable jobs with a typed diagnosis attached.
pitfalls: BullMQ requires thrown values to be Error objects; a thrown string or object is misclassified as a generic failure and weakens the diagnosis.
Stalled jobs also end up in the failed set, mixing 'worker died' with 'payload is invalid' - filter on the InvalidPayload type when reading or replaying.
Full job data (including personal data) is retained in Redis for failed jobs, so the invalid channel needs the same access control and retention policy as a broker error queue.
